content.rationale: The refine gives the shell a new use — the page's open request for a repo-relative content ref path — so an evaluation covering only the page (rtlotqvy) and the panel state (yruxqknp) no longer covers the shell's use of its prerequisites, and depends_on gains rptlovpt while keeping both. Layer and form, edge by edge: rtlotqvy (page and stylesheet) and yruxqknp (state module) are code-layer prerequisites and the shell is code, so those uses stay in the code-to-code cell's test form; rptlovpt is an inline prose commitment and the shell is code, which is the matrix's natural-to-code cell — fidelity — carried out here as the same runnable check because the dependent side is an artifact: the artifact must enforce exactly what the prose states, neither looser (a request naming a repo-relative path resolves inside the workspace root and opens that file) nor elsewhere (a path that does not resolve inside the root opens nothing and is reported as a failure). How the check observes, since the shell's own module is what it runs: src/panel.ts is compiled with the extension's esbuild into a file inside the extension — out/, removed as soon as it is loaded — because the extension host attributes the vscode a module requires to the file that module lives in, and a module loaded from outside the extension's files answers to the host's default API instance rather than the extension's. The check then opens the shell's panel on this repository, hands the panel the page's request at the webview's own message channel, and reads what the workbench did from the workbench's own records — the documents it opened, the documents it has open, the documents its editors show — rather than from window.activeTextEditor, which the workbench clears while an extension awaits and which says nothing about what is open or shown. A failure counts on either channel the host gives the shell, the workbench's message notifications or the message the page shows inline, because how a failure is reported is the shell's own. The request's shape is the interface this amendment introduces — no recorded node fixes a transport, message or command for it — so the check names that interface and nothing else of the shell's implementation: how the shell resolves the path, opens the document and reports the failure is its own. Matrix note, flagged for an entry: the natural-to-code cell is the fidelity form, realized as a runnable fidelity check because the child is an artifact. Amended for the unit that renames the extension in the manifest this decision refs: the shell identifies itself as deccy-viewer — package name and displayName, the command deccyViewer.openGraph, the webview view type deccyViewer.graph, the activation event and the menus — so the id the extension host installs it under is edawise.deccy-viewer (publisher and package name), and the check's lookup literal changes from edawise.vsc-deccy to edawise.deccy-viewer and nothing else: the same suites, the same assertions and the same observables, each of which resolves the extension under the id the manifest declares. The old literal pinned the pre-rename name, so it would have failed a correct rename while observing nothing the decision states; the amended check fails on a manifest that still declares the old name because the extension it observes is then not installed at all. Amended once more for the two prerequisites the shell's page use rests on, which the earlier amendments left uncovered: tpztomkv (the page composition — media/webview.html and the entry point src/webview/main.ts it loads) and nrwunqtx (the runner configuration vitest.config.ts that the extension-host suite sits beside) are code-layer prerequisites and the shell is code, so both uses are the code-to-code cell's test form, carried out in the same run. Reading the page the extension ships is not the same as observing the page the panel carries, so the check reads the webview's own html beside the file: the composition's markup is the markup the panel serves, and every reference the page declares is served as the file of the extension it names, resolved against the page's own directory through the workbench's webview URI, not left as the relative path the page carries. And because the run the check happens to be in says nothing about which runner brought it here, the check reads the two runner configurations as well: .vscode-test.mjs names a glob that files this suite for the extension host, and the include set of vitest.config.ts names no glob that claims it, so the shell's checks are the extension-host suites the split gives them and are not taken up a second time by the runner that has no extension host. Both uses went unread before: nothing the earlier gate ran had looked at the page the panel carried, and nothing it ran had read vitest.config.ts at all.
